SMTO-EXE-0257 — A tool this workflow uses is no longer available

GUID: 3922af61-d978-553e-99d5-e5b634a58771
Slug: recipe-step-tool-missing
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: recipes

What happened

  • This workflow needs a tool that SMTO can't find anymore. It may have been removed, renamed or turned off, for example by an update. SMTO stopped before using it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If the workflow used a skill you added yourself, open User Skills and check that it is still installed. The workflow looks up each tool by name when it starts, so a removed skill's tools can't be found.
  2. If SMTO was recently updated, open the conversation the workflow came from, select Save to workflow on your original message, then select Save workflow. A fresh save uses the tools SMTO has now.
  3. Before running the workflow again, check whether its earlier runs already made their changes. Running again could repeat a change that an earlier run already made.

What success looks like

  • The workflow runs without this message and its steps appear in the run's conversation.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the workflow's name, to the person who installed or manages SMTO; they can check whether the tool was removed in an update.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The registry lookup for a workflow step's tool failed, so the tool is missing from the current registry or its lookup raised an error.

What this means

  • A registry lookup for a captured or declared tool raised an exception; the tool may be absent or its registry lookup may have failed. Workflow diagnostics do not execute steps or grant approval. Preserve the pinned definition, original receipts, completed effects and any uncertainty; all execution uses the existing authorization boundary.

Why this can happen

  • A registry lookup for a captured or declared tool raised an exception; the tool may be absent or its registry lookup may have failed.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the exact canonical tool ID with the current registry and inspect the lookup failure before assuming installation is missing.

How to fix it

  • registry.get(step.canonical_tool_id) raised in validation.validate or recorder.extract, so the tool is missing from the runtime registry (capability policy does not affect this lookup). Restore the Skill or tool registration that provides it, or re-save the request as a saved-request workflow against the current registry.
  • Restore the intended tool registration or recapture a supported equivalent, then validate the workflow.

Retry and execution caution

  • Review the workflow and its current run evidence before retrying.

How to verify the fix

  • The exact tool resolves and its current contract validates the reviewed step.

What not to do

  • Never repeat a write whose effect remains unknown.

Technical notes

  • Workflow diagnostics do not execute steps or grant approval. Preserve the pinned definition, original receipts, completed effects and any uncertainty; all execution uses the existing authorization boundary.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
